findings.summary: Idempotence fails with the Bringhurst preset on, and with the en-US spaced-en-dash variant alone: a second pass changes the output, so fix-on-save stores a half-done fix, the audit lists the entry again right after the fix, and the next save changes stored content again. Three mechanisms are new in this delta: (a) D855’s spaced hyphen needs a word, number or closing mark before it, and its LEAD class has the curly ” ’ but not the straight " ', while dashes (priority 30) run before quotes (90), so `"Yes" - she said` is left on pass 1 and converted on pass 2; (b) under the preset, `---` in a locale whose break dash is not the closed em dash (en-GB, de, fr, it, …) becomes a settled em dash that typed-dashes (31) cannot restyle until pass 2; (c) spacedHyphens() and TypedDashesRule replace the spaces with the dash (` – ` settled), so widows cannot join a heading’s last word until pass 2 (the old `--` path replaced only the hyphens and is stable).

findings.summary: D858’s street guard for `St` reads the wrong bytes in two ways, so `Main St Louis` gets a no-break space or not depending on unrelated text, and a second pass under the DEFAULT rules can change the output. (a) apply() captures $text before the units and period-honorific passes, then gives afterStreetName() an offset into the edited run: after `10 kg` or `Dr. Watson` earlier in the run, the window ends one byte into `St` and the street is read as a saint. (b) the 48-byte window can start inside a multi-byte character; the /u preg_match then fails (returns false) and the guard reads “not a street”.
